interest: THNSL1 has not been directly implicated in stroke; it was only among >1,900 genes altered in mouse splenic B cells after protective hypoxic preconditioning, before stroke induction, with no functional follow-up.
NAA15 haploinsufficiency causes congenital heart disease, but hypertension was reported in only 1/19 evaluated individuals ascertained for truncating variants (Cheng H et al. 2018).
refs: Cheng H et al. 2018; Ward T et al. 2021

interest: OSBP knockdown increases cholesterol efflux in CHO cells and raises ABCA1 in J774 macrophages, providing a mechanistic link to HDL biology without direct human genetic evidence.

Podn-null mice show excessive neointimal lesion formation after arterial injury; overexpression of human PODN inhibits human vascular smooth-muscle-cell migration and proliferation, and PODN is expressed in human atheroma.
Cerebral ischemia recruits mSin3A to REST-corepressor complexes, providing mechanistic support without direct human genetic evidence for stroke.
IRS2 truncating variants increase chronic kidney disease risk independently of diabetes, and ghrelin-mediated protection from ischemic acute kidney injury is lost in Irs2-knockout mice.
refs: Zhao Y et al. 2025; Takeda R et al. 2006

interest: No retrieved literature directly links CPXM2 to rheumatoid arthritis; Open Targets provides low-confidence transcriptomic evidence of differential CPXM2 expression in rheumatoid arthritis and additional indirect support through ulcerative colitis, a related immune-mediated inflammatory disease.
No retrieved literature directly links SETD1A to asthma. Open Targets provides indirect support through forced expiratory volume, with a low evidence score (0.053).
